classification.difficultyReason: Select the sine area formula and apply the supplied sine derivative and angular rate before substituting the specified angle.

content.prompt:
In this triangle $ABC$, $\angle BAC$ is increasing at a constant rate of $0.2$ radians/s.

Use the fact that $\dfrac{d}{d\theta}(\sin\theta)=\cos\theta$ to find the rate of change in the area of $\triangle ABC$ when $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC has A at lower left, B above and C to the right; AC rises slightly. The included angle at A is theta with an increasing-angle directional cue.
spec.mathematics: AB=8 cm and AC=12 cm are fixed; angle BAC is theta and dtheta/dt=0.2 rad/s. The schematic angle is not a numerical given.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is supplied in the question.

answer.worked:
Using the sine area formula,
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12(AB)(AC)\sin\theta\\&=\frac12(8)(12)\sin\theta\\&=48\sin\theta.\end{aligned}$$
Since $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt}=0.2$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dA}{dt}&=48\cos\theta\frac{d\theta}{dt}\\&=48\cos\theta(0.2)\\&=9.6\cos\theta.\end{aligned}$$
When $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dA}{dt}&=9.6\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\\&=9.6\left(\frac12\right)\\&=4.8\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}.\end{aligned}$$
